clue.text: Design for a rude picture?

parts.note: blue means rude or risqué, as in a blue joke
a print is a picture made by printing, such as an engraving

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a plan is really just a smutty image.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: a 'rude picture' would be a blue print, run together into the word for a technical plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan drawn up for a building or machine is a synonym for a design.

clue.text: Jeers the accommodation provided for the fighters

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means heckles or jeers

definitions.text: the accommodation provided for the fighters
definitions.meaning: soldiers live in military quarters of that name

explanation.surface: Soldiers' quarters are mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: To heckle a speaker is a verb sense; as a noun it is housing for soldiers.

clue.text: Arrangements to ensure four are protected from creation

indicators.note: the four is shielded inside the rearranged letters
the letters of ensure are put into new arrangements

parts.note: taken as written
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Plans to keep a quartet safe from the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangements' looks like a noun, but it signals the anagram, giving UNERSE; 'are protected' tucks the Roman numeral inside.
explanation.definitionFit: All that exists, the whole of creation, is the cosmos.

clue.text: Almost inclined to be quick

indicators.note: almost the whole word, losing its last letter

parts.note: prone means inclined or liable
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is nearly disposed to hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronto is informal for promptly, quickly, at once.

clue.text: Locked up at home with the team

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: Someone is confined indoors with their teammates.
explanation.definitionFit: In jail is informally described as inside.

clue.text: Looking for a lift, okay?

definitions.meaning: hitchhikers signal for a ride with a raised thumb
the gesture is also asked or given as a sign of approval

explanation.surface: A hitchhiker asks if all is well.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised-thumb gesture signals both hitching a ride and agreement.

clue.text: Saw a vessel overwhelmed by them

indicators.note: the answer is swamped, swallowed up, by the run of letters in the words saw a vessel

explanation.surface: Someone saw a ship swamped by the sea's surges.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside sAW A VESsel. 'them' is the definition, pointing to what swamps a ship at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakers and swells are what overwhelm a ship, so the pronoun stands for them.

clue.text: Angry snake runs from pig

parts.note: wild means furious, angry
a boa is a constricting snake
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A furious serpent flees from a swine.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild swine of Europe and Asia is a kind of pig.

clue.text: Free from tax, accepted container

indicators.note: the tax takes in, accepts, the container inside it

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax
a can is a container

explanation.surface: A tax-exempt shipping container was waved through.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is Britain's value added tax, a sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat or room that is unoccupied is free, available.

clue.text: Alone, man is disheartened and serious

parts.note: sole means only, alone

indicators.note: losing its heart, the word man keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A lonely man, dejected, looks grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' looks like sadness; it removes the middle letter A from MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and earnest in manner is solemn.

clue.text: No American follows game — one causing injury

indicators.note: follows puts the words no American after game and one in the answer

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union, a ball game
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
US is short for the United States, hence American

explanation.surface: A rejected American comes after a game, and someone gets hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: RU stands for rugby union. The dash makes 'one' look like the start of the definition, but it gives I, and 'follows' puts the 'No American' pieces after the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disastrous or destructive does harm, so it is damaging.

clue.text: I am to act as broker if urgent

parts.note: contracted, I am becomes I'm
a broker goes between parties, so to act as one is to mediate

explanation.surface: Someone offers to negotiate a deal if it is pressing.
explanation.definitionFit: An urgent matter needs dealing with at once, without delay.

clue.text: Stick through the heart? Rot!

indicators.note: the stick is pushed through the middle, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: the core of something is its heart
a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: A dismissive retort to talk of driving a stake through someone's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rot!' looks like an exclamation of disbelief but is the verb to decay.
explanation.definitionFit: To corrode is to eat away or decay, the sense of rot as a verb.

clue.text: Others are different with new cut

indicators.note: the letters of others are made different, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Other people look different after a fresh haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are different' rearranges OTHERS into SHORTE, then N is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim something reduces its length, so cut means make less long.

clue.text: Would one invest in an idle husband?

definitions.text: Would one invest in an idle husband?

parts.words: Would one invest in an idle husband?
parts.note: an investor who puts money into a business but takes no active part, read jokily as a spouse who lies in bed

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether anyone would back a lazy spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A silent backer of a firm puts in capital without working there; literally, a bedfellow who is dozing.

clue.text: Rehearse part of the play within cost

indicators.note: within puts the part of the play inside the word for cost

parts.note: price means cost
an act is a division of a play

explanation.surface: Run through a scene, staying on budget.
explanation.definitionFit: To practise or drill is to rehearse; the US spelling serves as the verb.

clue.text: Propose a short letter about main changes

indicators.note: the note goes around the other letters

parts.note: a note is a brief letter

indicators.note: the word main changes its order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a brief memo about major revisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' gives MINA, and 'about' wraps the short letter round it; 'Propose' means put forward a name.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward a candidate is to propose or put up someone.

clue.text: Negotiate via agent for sail

indicators.note: to negotiate the letters is to work them round into a new order

explanation.surface: Arrange through a representative for a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Negotiate' looks like the definition, but here it shuffles VIA AGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer a ship's course over water is to sail.

clue.text: Area 51 is covered — that's the belief!

indicators.note: the numeral is covered, enclosed, by the word for area

parts.note: a region is an area
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A conspiracy theorist insists the Nevada base is being hushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: Area 51 is the secret US base; split it, and LI is Roman 51.
explanation.definitionFit: A faith or creed is a system of belief.

clue.text: Bill to demand the right of approval

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
to claim something is to demand it as one's right

explanation.surface: A proposed law seeks to make approval a matter of entitlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a parliamentary bill; it is an account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclaim is enthusiastic praise or public applause, a strong form of approval.

clue.text: Approach a hundred at a price

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
cost means price

explanation.surface: Someone approaches with a hundred at a set price.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to go up and speak to them boldly.

clue.text: Fearful of having caught a blackbird

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a raven is a black bird

explanation.surface: Someone is afraid of a crow-like bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowardly or timid is craven.

clue.text: A French individual in Rome adds 104 to 49 and gets rude

parts.note: un is French for a, or one individual
CIV is 104 in Roman numerals
IL is a loose Roman form of 49, one before fifty

explanation.surface: A mock arithmetic problem set in ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Rome' tells you the numbers are Roman numerals: C (100) + IV (4) = CIV, and IL is one less than L (50).
explanation.definitionFit: Being impolite or discourteous is being rude.

clue.text: Loose, German and single

parts.note: und is German for and
one means single

explanation.surface: A German who is unattached and free.
explanation.definitionFit: Untied, as of a knot or shoelace, means loose.

clue.text: Lose energy in stopping shell

indicators.note: lose means the letter for energy is taken out

parts.note: ceasing means stopping
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Run out of steam when halting an artillery shell.
explanation.definitionFit: An outer covering, such as of a sausage or cartridge, is a shell.

clue.text: Suitably told off, Charlie got a move on

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to get a move on is to hurry, hastened

explanation.surface: Charlie was scolded and hurried off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rebuked and made humble has been chastened.

clue.text: Most beginning to accept early art from Japan

indicators.note: the shortened word takes in, accepts, another piece inside it
most of the word means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: an origin is a beginning
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning, early in the day

explanation.surface: Most early Japanese art is thought to have started a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' drops the last letter of the word for beginning, giving ORIGI; 'to accept' puts the morning abbreviation inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper folding is a traditional Japanese craft.

clue.text: A hint of money, say, coming back

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

indicators.note: the abbreviation for say is read in reverse order

parts.note: EG, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A suggestion that cash may be returning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' reverses EG to GE. TIN as money is old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace or tint, so a hint of something.

clue.text: Always popular, but the first lady to run without experience

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in the Bible
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
green means inexperienced, new to the job

explanation.surface: An enduring favourite, though the leading lady is a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lady' suggests a president's wife, but it is Eve of Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: A song or show that never goes out of fashion is called an evergreen.
